recentItems.title: The DESTINY of Europe is DECIDED HERE! Zelenskyy on DEFENDERS’ DAY at the front
recentItems.description:
On the Day of Defenders and Defendresses of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelenskyy recorded an address not among capital symbols, but directly on the frontline. The President emphasized: it is precisely among camouflage nets, military positions, and command posts that the history of Ukraine is being written today and the fate of its independence is being decided.

The Head of State remembered the fallen heroes and the words of warrior and poet Maksym Kryvtsov: “When they ask me what war is, I will answer without hesitation: names.” On the 1,681st day of the full-scale war, Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked everyone defending the country — from infantrymen and artillerymen to pilots, drone operators, intelligence officers, and engineers.

The President of Ukraine is convinced that the path to peace lies precisely through the resilience of the people holding the frontline today.

This video is about those who “carry Ukraine's Independence on their shoulders,” and the price Ukraine pays for the right to remain itself.

recentItems.title: Ukraine to GET New F-16s & Patriots as Europe RESPONDS to Russian Intelligence
recentItems.description:
A Russian Tu-95 strategic bomber has crashed in Russia's Amur Oblast. According to reports, six out of seven crew members were killed, and one was hospitalized. The official cause of the crash has not yet been established. At the same time, reports are coming in regarding a massive drone attack on the Belgorod region and fuel shortages in areas near Moscow following strikes on Russian oil refineries.

Meanwhile, Ukraine is bolstering its air defense: Belgium is set to deliver three more F-16s by the end of the year, while the UK has announced a £100 million aid package including Patriot interceptor missiles, artillery ammunition, and drones. This episode also highlights the first reported interception of a jet-powered "Geran-4" by the Ukrainian "General Chereshnya Bullet" drone.

Simultaneously, tensions are mounting in Europe. The EU is considering listing Russia's GRU as a terrorist organization, Estonia reports sabotage at a defense facility, and NATO warns of increasingly brazen Russian hybrid operations. Moscow is also threatening escalation around Kaliningrad, while NATO reiterates its commitment to continued support for Ukraine.

recentItems.title: Russia STRIKES Ukraine's Energy Grid, Poland&Romania Scramble Aircraft, Jet Drone Crashes in Moldova
recentItems.description:
Russia has launched its largest attack on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure since the end of the previous heating season. In Kyiv, three people were reported killed and six injured, with residential buildings, a store, and other facilities damaged. Emergency power outages have hit parts of the capital and several regions following the grid strikes, with generating equipment damaged at the Trypilska Thermal Power Plant. Amid the barrage, Poland and Romania scrambled military aircraft, while Moldova reported the crash and explosion of a jet-powered drone.

On the front lines, Operation "Vivaldi" continues: according to reports in this episode, the 66th Mechanized Brigade, together with other units of the 3rd Army Corps, has reclaimed over 125 km² of Ukrainian territory. Over 24 hours, the General Staff recorded 221 combat engagements, while the Defense Forces struck Russian drone depots, a command post, a repair base, and supply facilities.

The episode also covers the dire humanitarian situation in occupied Oleshky, which Ukraine is bringing before an urgent OSCE meeting, as well as reports of Russian forces confiscating aid delivered to local residents by Ukrainian drones. Additionally, PACE has documented crimes against Ukrainian journalists and passed resolutions on media protection and veteran support. Finally, we break down discussions around a potential halt to energy grid strikes, the stance of the US and Germany, and calls from American lawmakers to maintain sanction pressure on Russia.

recentItems.title: Russia CAUSES GENOCIDE – HORRIFIC humanitarian catastrophe in OLESHKY
recentItems.description:
The town of Oleshky in Southern Ukraine. Occupied territory. The settlement, where thousands of people remain, is virtually under a blockade: roads are mined, drones fly constantly, and civilians live under the threat of shelling and attacks by the occupiers.

In Oleshky, electricity, water, gas, communications, fuel, food, and medical aid are almost non-existent, and due to a lack of generator fuel, the hospital cannot perform complex surgeries. Because of mined roads and relentless attacks, aid barely arrives, people suffer from hunger, and Russian occupiers even seize humanitarian food supplies and target those who receive them.

Witnesses describe Oleshky as a place where people have lost all sense of safety and dignity, yet still hold on to the hope of returning home.

recentItems.description:
The Kremlin is still not ready to end the war — this is confirmed by both President Zelenskyy and the Chairman of the Bundestag Foreign Affairs Committee, Johann Wadephul, following his meeting with Lavrov. Putin is searching for new excuses to continue his aggression, accusing Ukraine of striking civilian infrastructure "first," even though Russia started doing so back in 2022. Moscow rejects an energy truce and is ramping up drone production for 2027, planning to spend $12 billion on jet-powered Shaheds alone. ISW analysts believe Putin is betting on terrorist strikes against Ukraine's energy grid this winter. For the Kremlin, the war has become a core element of domestic politics, without which it would be difficult to justify restrictions and costs to its citizens.

NATO and the EU emphasized that the Kremlin's hybrid attacks and sabotage in Europe will only strengthen the allies' resolve to provide military assistance to Ukraine.
